etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French collectif, from Latin collēctīvus, from collēctus, past participle of colligō (“I collect”), from com- (“together”) + legō (“I gather”). Compare French collectif. Doublet of colectivo.

definitions.definition: Formed by gathering or collecting; gathered into a mass, sum, or body.
Tending to collect; forming a collection.

quote.citation: 1743, [Edward Young], “Night the Fourth. The Christian Triumph.”, in The Complaint: Or, Night-Thoughts on Life, Death, and Immortality, London:  […]  R[obert] Dodsley, […], →OCLC, page 18:
quote.text: Local is his throne  […]  to fix a point, / A central point, collective of his sons.

definitions.definition: Having plurality of origin or authority.
(grammar) Expressing a collection or aggregate of individuals, by a singular form.

quote.citation: 1642, Tho[mas] Browne, “(please specify the page)”, in Religio Medici. […], 4th edition, London:  […]  E. Cotes for Andrew Crook […], published 1656, →OCLC:

definitions.definition: A farm owned by a collection of people.
(especially in communist countries) One of more farms managed and owned, through the state, by the community.
(by extension) A group dedicated to a particular cause or interest.

quote.citation: 2005, Zoya Kocur, Simon Leung, Theory in contemporary art since 1985, page 76:
quote.text: There are, however, a number of contemporary artists and art collectives that have defined their practice precisely around the facilitation of dialogue among diverse communities.

quote.citation: 2006 March 5, Holland Cotter, “The Collective Conscious”, in The New York Times‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: Critical Art Ensemble is one of many art collectives operating on the principle that information is power and that it is most effectively made available through a combination of science and aesthetics.

quote.citation: 2021 October 13, Adam Bradley, “The Creative Collectives Finding Strength in Numbers”, in The New York Times‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: Today’s collectives create together, tour together, exhibit together, live together, survive together, eat together, sleep together, march together, fight together and party together, too.

definitions.definition: The flight control used to control a helicopter's ascent or descent.

quote.citation: 2012, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Helicopter Flying Handbook: FAA-H-8083-21A, Ravenio Books:
quote.text: A pilot normally holds the collective stationary until the helicopter stops; however, to get more braking action, lower the collective slightly. Keep in mind that, due to the increased ground friction when the collective is lowered or […]

quote.citation: 2021 July 27, Federal Aviation Administration, Helicopter Flying Handbook: FAA-H-8083-21B, Simon and Schuster, →ISBN:
quote.text: Hover height, rate of ascent, and the rate of descent are controlled by using the collective. Helicopter position and the direction of travel are controlled by the cyclic.
